title: What Is Good Enough to Move Forward?
scene: You have reduced the important uncertainty. Now you need to decide whether the evidence is strong enough to act.
sceneJa: 重要な不確実性をある程度減らしたあと、完璧な情報を待つのではなく、次の行動を支えるだけの根拠があるかを判断する場面。

chunks.ja: 完璧な情報がそろっていることは、めったにありません

chunks.en: when we need to make a decision.
chunks.ja: 判断を下さなければならないときに
確実になるまで待つのではなく

chunks.en: whether the evidence is strong enough
chunks.ja: 根拠が十分に強いかどうか
次の段階へ進む判断を支えられるほどに
その答えは〜によって変わります
何が懸かっているのか

chunks.en: and how difficult the decision would be
chunks.ja: そして、その判断がどれほど難しいか
間違えた場合の代償が大きいほど

questions.question: Which chunking is most natural?
options: whether the evidence is strong enough / to support the next step
whether the evidence / is strong / enough to support / the next step
whether / the evidence is strong enough to / support the next / step
questions.explanation: ‘Strong enough’ forms the judgment, and ‘to support the next step’ explains what it is strong enough to do.

questions.question: What does ‘what is at stake’ mean here?
options: What could be gained or lost because of the decision.
How long the meeting will take.
questions.explanation: ‘At stake’ refers to what could be gained, lost, or put at risk by the decision.

questions.question: According to the passage, when should we require stronger evidence?
options: When a mistake would be costly or difficult to reverse.
questions.explanation: Higher-cost or less reversible decisions justify a higher standard of evidence.

speak: Build toward the final sentence as if it were a decision rule. Stress ‘more costly’ and ‘stronger’ so the relationship is clear: ‘The more costly the mistake, the stronger the evidence we should require.’
review: Previous session: ‘we do not need to resolve all of them now’, ‘relevant to the next step’, and ‘reduce enough of it’. Today asks the next question: once the relevant uncertainty has been reduced, is the evidence strong enough to act? The required strength depends on what is at stake and how reversible the decision is.
